title: Integration of 3D Mixed Reality Technologies into Preoperative Assessment and Surgical Planning for Pelvic Sarcomas
summary:
Background

Surgery is often the primary treatment for malignant bone and soft-tissue tumors in the pelvic region. Such procedures are challenging because many blood vessels, nerves, and organs are closely packed together in the pelvis. To help patients fully understand their condition and the planned surgery, they have typically been shown two-dimensional cross-sectional images from computed tomography scans. However, for people without prior medical knowledge, it is difficult to visualize the actual location and size of a tumor within the body based on such flat images.

In this study, special glasses are used that allow patients to view a three-dimensional model of the tumor and the surrounding body structures as if they were floating objects in space. This model is created in advance using the existing CT images. The technology combines the real environment with additional virtual images that can be controlled through hand and voice gestures.

Research Question

The study investigates whether such a three-dimensional visualization helps patients better understand their condition and the upcoming surgery, thereby reducing their anxiety about the procedure. It also examines whether the surgeons find the three-dimensional models helpful during preparation and during the surgery, and whether this affects their workload.

Methodology

The study includes adult patients who are scheduled for surgery due to a pelvic tumor. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group receives, in addition to the standard information session, an expanded explanation using the 3D model viewed through the glasses. The other group receives the standard information session without this technology.

Before and after the preoperative consultation, all participants complete questionnaires designed to assess their understanding and levels of anxiety. Participants in the group using the glasses also complete a questionnaire about their experience with this technology. After the surgery, the operating physicians also use questionnaires to evaluate how helpful the visualization was to them and how much additional work it required. The standard imaging tests and medical treatment remain unchanged by the study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Planned extensive or radical resection or reconstructive surgery in the pelvic region
- Availability of clinically indicated cross-sectional imaging (computed tomography) for the creation of the 3D model
- Written informed consent
- Sufficient knowledge of German to understand the information provided and to complete the questionnaires
Exclusion criteria:
- Inability to give informed consent
- Lack of or withdrawal of consent
- Insufficient knowledge of German to understand the informed consent form and complete the questionnaires
- Lack of suitable cross-sectional imaging to create the 3D model
- Medical or technical contraindications to the use of the mixed-reality headset (e.g., relevant visual impairment that prevents viewing the model, or conditions under which wearing the headset is not reasonable)
